description: We are a small, friendly team based in Seoul, and we’re looking for a few more people to join us for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our focus is on using data, Python, and simple machine learning to turn NASA’s open data into something useful and easy to understand.
summary:
Field Shift is an autonomous edge intelligence station deployed on a micro-controller, that bridges global satellite climatology coupled with root-level ground telemetry directly at the farm gate. We utilize the dual-core Tuya T5AI IoT micro-controller and the open-source TuyaOpen framework. The system connects over WiFi/TLS to the open NASA POWER API, importing regional surface wetness, root-zone moisture, weekly precipitation, and minimum temperatures without the use of API keys. 

By the evaluation of satellite land-surface models againts in-situ capacitive soil and weather probes in real-time, our project calculates micro-climate divergence (namely, soil and temperature gap), tracks live Pearson correlation (r), and computes  an actionable, multi-factor Irrigation Need Index. Crucial agronomic decisions, such as front warnings and irrigation urgency, are rendered on an interactive LCD touchscreen featuring an organic interface.

Field Shift utilizes NASA Earth Observations for resource-constrained small landholders. By factoring in deep subsoil reserves and recent rainfall, it conserves a substantial percentage of agricultural freshwater, prevents crop loss from unexpected frost, and delivers space science directly to the farmers feeding all of humanity!
details:
What It Does and How Does It Function?

Field Shift is a self-contained, low-power agricultural console installed anywhere in the field with a reliable power source. It operates a continuous multi-tasking edge pipeline running on FreeRTOS:

  • Direct-to-NASA Telemetry Ingestion: Every 3 hours, an embedded TLS client queries the open NASA POWER API (power.larc.nasa.gov), stream-parsing ~2.2 KB JSON payloads containing GMAO MERRA-2 and GEOS-IT agro-meteorology parameters (GWETTOP, GWETROOT, PRECTOTCORR, T2M, T2M_MIN, RH2M). Lacking an RTC or external NTP daemon, it extracts the standard HTTP Date header from the response to synchronize the system clock with zero network overhead.
    • Soil Gap: Local Soil−NASA Surface Wetness, detecting localized drought or poor drainage.
    • Temperature Gap: Local Temp−NASA 2m Air Temp, detecting sheltered frost pockets or greenhouse heat traps.
    • Pearson Correlation (r): Computed across a rolling 16-pair buffer to verify whether the field naturally tracks regional climatology or has decoupled due to irrigation.
    • Multi-Factor Irrigation Need Index (0−1000 - 1000−100): Combines baseline soil deficit with a 7-day cumulative rainfall offset and NASA root-zone subsoil buffering, producing unambiguous verdicts: "No Irrigation Needed", "Advisable Soon", or "Irrigate Now".
  • Predictive Forecasting & Alarms: An on-device Damped Holt Linear Smoothing model (ϕ=0.97) projects 24-step soil drying curves hours ahead, while an industrial alarm engine with de-bounced hold times, hysteresis, and acoustic chimes triggers alerts for frost risks, heat stress, and sensor-lost timeouts.

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Zero Recurring Fees: Fully autonomous and runs locally on open-source firmware and free NASA public data, eliminating expensive cellular IoT subscriptions.
  • Deep Subsoil Awareness: Prevents premature, wasteful watering when topsoil looks dry but NASA confirms the deep root zone (0–100 cm) is sufficiently moist.
  • Early Frost Warning: Flags regional minimum temperature drops (T2M_MIN) before localized frost forms in sheltered farm hollows.
  • Cognitive Calm: Replaces cluttered, high-stress neon industrial dashboards with an organic, calming aesthetic designed for quick glanceability in bright sunlight.

Intended Impact

  • Freshwater Conservation: Reduces agricultural water usage by factoring in deep root-zone buffers and recent multi-day rainfall.
  • Economic Democratization: At cheap Bill of Materials (BoM), Field Shift makes precision agriculture accessible to smallholder farmers worldwide who are priced out of $500+ commercial weather stations.
  • Translating Space Science into Action: Translates complex, coarse numerical weather models into direct, field-level decisions without requiring farmers to have a degree in meteorology or data science.

Hardware & Software Stack

  • Hardware:
    • SoC: Tuya T5AI Development Board (T5-BOARD-35565LCD), featuring the Beken BK7258 Dual-Core ARM Cortex-M33 processor with Wi-Fi 6, BLE 5.4, hardware audio DAC, and PSRAM.
    • Display & Touch: 3.5" TFT LCD, 480×320 landscape orientation (ILI9488 RGB565 driver) with Goodix GT1151 I2C capacitive touch controller.
    • Sensors: Analog capacitive soil moisture probe v1.2 (ADC), DHT22/SHT3x digital temperature & humidity probe (GPIO), ambient lux sensor.
    • Acoustics & Enclosure: On-board speaker for alarm chime sequences; custom 3D-printable landscape weather-resistant enclosure.
    • Languages: Embedded C (C99/C11), FreeRTOS.
    • SDK & Build: TuyaOpen IoT SDK, tos.py, CMake, Ninja, GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain (gcc-arm-none-eabi).
    • Libraries: LVGL v8/v9 Embedded GUI Library, mbedTLS / Tuya IoT TLS client, cJSON streaming parser.
    • NASA POWER API (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) delivering GMAO MERRA-2 and GEOS-IT agro-climatology reanalysis models.

Novelty of Field Shift

  • Edge-Native Macro/Micro Fusion: Instead of simply plugging in and displaying raw sensor numbers, Field Shift innovatively fuses high-altitude space observations with in-situ root sensors right inside an edge microcontroller.
  • The Studio Ghibli Aesthetic: Agricultural IoT interfaces are traditionally cold, harsh, and stressful. Field Shift deviates by adopting a warm, organic visual language inspired by Studio Ghibli films, featuring soft pasture tones, custom pixel art, and an animated leaf sprite generated by GenAI tools.
  • Zero-Overhead Clock Sync: Replaces bulky NTP daemons with a clever zero-overhead clock synchronization mechanism that parses the HTTP Date header returned during NASA TLS handshakes.
  • Ethical Simulation Transparency: Features persistent visual SIM badges on the screen whenever synthetic sensor drivers are active, ensuring total honesty during demonstrations.

Factors We Considered

  • Memory & Reliability Constraints: Since we are operating on a heavily constrained edge system, we required zero dynamic heap allocation in steady-state. Telemetry history is quantized into 16-bit fixed-point (q16) integers across static buffers, locking free system RAM at ~168 KB with zero risk of heap fragmentation crashes over months of operation.
  • Satellite Data Latency: Satellite assimilation products (MERRA-2) have a 2-to-3-day publication lag. We implemented a sliding 14-day temporal window that scans backwards day-by-day to ingest the newest valid record, while transparently labeling the exact dataset date on-screen.
  • Rural Network Realities: Agricultural Wi-Fi is notoriously unstable. We engineered an exponential backoff state machine (30 s→15 min) and multi-tier fallbacks (subsoil fallback to surface wetness; full offline fallback to synthetic diurnal generators).
  • Sensor Drift & Physical Failure: Ground probes degrade over time. We implemented sensor-lost watchdog timers (lost_ms), out-of-range gating (min_valid/max_valid), and time-debounced alarm hysteresis to prevent false alarms from electrical noise or contact resistance.
